citations.quote:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $E$ be a smooth real rank-$2m$ vector bundle on $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$, $m\ge1$, with a smooth endomorphism $J$ satisfying $J^2=-I$. On the two boundary edges let $F_0,F_1$ be smooth real rank-$m$ subbundles with $F_j\cap JF_j=0$. Suppose that outside a compact strip there are specified smooth complex frames $\tau_\pm:\mathbb C^m\to E$, intertwining $i$ and $J$, in which $F_0=\mathbb R^m$ and $F_1=i\mathbb R^m$. Let $P$ be a smooth real linear first-order operator on sections of $E$ with symbol
$$P(f\xi)=fP\xi+f_s\xi+f_tJ\xi$$
for every smooth real function $f$, and suppose its expression in each end frame is exactly $\partial_s+i\partial_t$ outside a compact strip.

There exist a global smooth complex frame $\Phi$, a sign matrix $S_+=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma,1,\ldots,1)$ with $\sigma\in\{1,-1\}$, an integer $\ell$, and a smooth real function $\vartheta(s)$, constant at $\pi/2$ on the negative end and $\pi/2+\ell\pi$ on the positive end, such that $\Phi=\tau_-$ on the negative end, $\Phi=\tau_+S_+$ on the positive end, and
$$F_0=\Phi\mathbb R^m,\qquad F_1=\Phi\left(e^{i\vartheta(s)}\mathbb R\times i\mathbb R^{m-1}\right).$$
In this frame $P$ is $\partial_s+i\partial_t+B(s,t)$ with smooth compactly supported real linear $B$. On the $H^1$ completion of compactly supported smooth sections satisfying those actual boundary subbundles, with the norm defined by finite bundle charts on a compact core and the prescribed frames on the ends, $P$ maps to the corresponding $L^2(E)$ space and is real Fredholm, with
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}P=-\ell.$$
The same index holds with the weight $e^{\delta|s|}$ for $0\le\delta<\pi/2$. These are indices before any translation quotient. The integer $\ell$ is independent of the choices in the construction, since it is minus the index of this fixed operator.

In particular the conclusion applies to the actual linearization at a smooth $J_t$-holomorphic strip of finite Dirichlet energy, measured in a smooth target metric, in a compact target, with compact totally real boundary submanifolds of transverse finite intersection, whenever the chosen target charts at their intersections identify those submanifolds with $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t$ with the constant structure $i$ for every $t$. For product Heegaard tori such a geometric choice is available by the product-integrable generator-neighborhood construction. No domain Euler-measure formula, corner/excision theorem, generic regularity, or moduli count is part of this conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice. Consider an actual smooth complex rank-$m$ strip bundle, totally real horizontal boundary subbundles, specified end frames identifying these subbundles with $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$, and a smooth real first-order operator with Cauchy–Riemann symbol and exact expression $\partial_s+i\partial_t$ in those frames outside a compact set. Its index means the real Fredholm index before source translation, on fixed-end $H^{q+1}\to H^q$ spaces, for an integer $q\ge0$.

Take a compact strip rectangle $Q$ containing the nonconstant part. Complete the horizontal boundary subbundles to a totally real loop along $\partial Q$ using the vertical end caps
$$L_\pm(t)=\tau_\pm e^{i\pi\rho(t)/2}\mathbb R^m,$$
where $\rho:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ is smooth, zero near zero, one near one, and increases from zero to one. The boundary orientation is that induced by $ds\wedge dt$. In any smooth global complex frame on $Q$, a local real basis $v_1,\ldots,v_m$ of this loop defines
$$\zeta=\frac{(\det_{\mathbb C}(v_1,\ldots,v_m))^2}{|\det_{\mathbb C}(v_1,\ldots,v_m)|^2}\in S^1.$$
These local expressions agree on overlaps. Its integer winding $M$ is independent of real bases, global complex frame, sufficiently large rectangle, and cap cutoff $\rho$, and
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}P=M.$$
The equality also holds with smooth two-sided weights below the end spectral gap $\pi/2$. This specifies actual caps and signs, rather than defining an unexplained topological index.

The following finite-dimensional excision and model calculations hold with the same squared determinant convention.

* Direct sums add $M$. Gluing two such strip problems with matching product end frames and operators exactly constant near the cut adds their actual real indices. This is a statement about the glued linear boundary problem.
* On a rectangle with finitely many disjoint round interior disks removed, suppose a continuous totally real subbundle in a trivial complex bundle is defined on the remaining compact surface. Then the determinant winding along the outer boundary is the sum of its windings along the positively counterclockwise hole circles. It suffices that the bundle be smooth near the boundary circles; for a smooth bundle the local windings can be computed by the following models.
* For the symmetric-coordinate map $q(z_1,z_2)=(z_1+z_2,z_1z_2)$, transport the two real lines generated by the same nonzero constant $v\in\mathbb C$ along $z_1=-\sqrt w,z_2=\sqrt w$, $w$ traversing a small counterclockwise circle. Their image under $dq$ has squared determinant winding $+1$. More generally an order-$r$ source-cover model consisting of the $r$ roots of $w$, with the same constant source vector on each sheet and elementary symmetric target coordinates, has winding $r-1$.
* A scalar target map $f(z)=z^{r+1}$, on a sheet unbranched over the parameter disk, sends a nonzero constant real direction to a line of squared phase winding $2r$ along a positive source circle.
* For two graph branches $(z,Az),(z,Bz)$ in $\mathbb C\times\mathbb C$, with $A,B:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^2$ real linear invertible and $A-B$ invertible, choose source directions $A^{-1}v,B^{-1}v$ for a fixed nonzero $v\in\mathbb C$. Push their target directions to the symmetric coordinates of $Az,Bz$. The resulting two-plane has squared determinant winding $2\operatorname{sign}\det_{\mathbb R}(A-B)$. This sign equals the oriented intersection sign of the two graph sheets, both oriented by their $z$ coordinate and the product oriented by base then target.
* A scalar source direction winding $k$ on an otherwise nonsingular sheet contributes $2k$ to the squared determinant winding. Extra fixed nonzero product directions change none of these local contributions.

These assertions do not identify the domain Euler measure or corner multiplicities of an arbitrary Whitney class. In particular, no representativity theorem, collapsed-tube calculation, corner rounding formula, or branched-cover Euler identity is included.

derivations.claim:
Choose any smooth connection $
abla$ on $TX$ to express the actual covariant linearization of the Cauchy–Riemann section at $u$, including when its value is nonzero. Its formula is $$P_u\xi=
abla_s\xi+J_t(u)
abla_t\xi+(
abla_\xi J_t)(u)u_t.$$ This follows by differentiating the section using that connection on its target bundle; a torsion-free connection gives the displayed formula, and any other connection alters it by a smooth zeroth-order term only. One can instead define this displayed Cauchy–Riemann-symbol operator directly with a torsion-free connection; the index conclusion for all such choices is the same. A smooth connection needed here is supplied by a finite target-chart partition on compact $X$: take flat torsion-free chart connections and their finite smooth partition sum. It is torsion-free because torsion is affine in a connection, and it obeys the connection rule because the weights sum to one. On a constant tail $du=0$, its expression in the fixed target chart is exactly $\partial_s+i\partial_t$. Its symbol is $P_u(f\xi)=fP_u\xi+f_s\xi+f_tJ_t(u)\xi$. The pulled-back horizontal tangent bundles are totally real by the endpoint hypotheses on $J_0,J_1$. Thus the general bundle-operator theorem [F1] applies and proves actual Fredholmness on the fixed-end completion. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

Consider the stated smooth homotopy. On the compact box $[0,1]_h\times[-R,R]_s\times[0,1]_t$ containing all nonconstant parts, $H^*TX$ with complex structure $J_t(H)$ has a global smooth complex frame. Here are the parameter details of the finite construction in [F1]. Choose finitely many complex local frames and supported smooth scalar bumps whose squared sum is positive, and embed a fiber by the list of its bump-weighted frame coordinates into one fixed $\mathbb C^N$. This has smooth image projection $Q=V(V^*V)^{-1}V^*$ in every local image-column matrix $V$. Along the straight radial segments from one point of the box, transport an initial complex basis by $Z'=[Q',Q]Z$. Differentiating $Q^2=Q$ shows that this transport preserves the image and inner products. The iterated-integral series has bounds $M^n/n!$; every fixed parameter derivative adds only polynomial factors in $n$, so it converges smoothly in all three parameters on this compact box. Pull the transported vectors back to obtain the asserted joint frame. This supplies one family of frames on the entire homotopy, instead of choosing unrelated frames for uncountably many slices. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

Its index is the boundary-phase winding in [F2]. The boundary planes and the product end caps depend on $u,J_t,L_j$, not on the connection. Changing the connection changes no one of these planes or caps and hence leaves this winding unchanged. All such operators satisfy the exact end hypothesis in step 1.1, so this proves connection independence by their actual Fredholm index formula. It does not infer smoothness of a nonlinear count or use an index formula for a formal region chain. [F2, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

For each $h$, complete the horizontal tangent subbundles around the same rectangle by the product-chart vertical caps $e^{i\pi\rho(t)/2}\mathbb R^m$ from [F2]. These caps are the same geometric planes for every $h$, since the ends and their charts were fixed. In the joint frame of step 1.2 the squared determinant phase is one continuous map from $[0,1]\times\partial Q$ to $S^1$. It is well defined even without orienting the horizontal real bundles: a real basis change has nonzero real determinant, whose normalized square is one. Local real frames exist smoothly in both variables by their local bundle coordinates. The phase therefore gives a genuine loop homotopy. Homotopy invariance of winding in [F2] makes its integer constant in $h$. The actual index formula applied separately at each slice proves index invariance for this actual smooth homotopy. [F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

Concatenate representatives $u:x\to y$ and $v:y\to z$ by translating their nonconstant cores into successive intervals and identifying their constant $y$ collars. They agree with all derivatives on the joined constant region, so the result is smooth, with the original boundary conditions and exact outer tails. The actual bundle operators of step 1.1 also agree with $D_0$ in their common generator chart there. The exact-end linear gluing assertion [F2] therefore makes the index of this concatenation the sum of the two indices. Extending or deleting a finite constant collar inserts or removes boundary planes and matching caps with opposite phase changes, so it does not change the integer. At a constant representative all horizontal planes are constant in its single product chart; the two vertical cap phase changes cancel, giving winding and index zero. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

The reversed representative $\bar u(s,t)=u(-s,t)$ satisfies the same totally real boundary conditions with ends interchanged. Choose a frame for $u$ on a large rectangle and pull it back by $(s,t)\mapsto(-s,t)$ for $\bar u$. Its completed boundary loop is exactly the original loop precomposed with this orientation-reversing reflection: the positive and negative vertical caps are exchanged with their geometric product frames, while the horizontal plane data are reflected. A positively oriented boundary traversal therefore makes the opposite total phase change. Thus [F2] gives $\operatorname{ind}P_{\bar u}=-\operatorname{ind}P_u$. Together with steps 2.2 and 3.1 this proves all the smooth quotient, constant, concatenation and reversal assertions. No step asserted that an arbitrary continuous relative class had already been smoothed, or equated this integer with a domain Euler/corner expression. Those remain separate prerequisites for a full continuous Whitney-class comparison. [F2, step 2.2, step 3.1, construct, algebra] ∎

boundaries.reason: The Statement assumes actual rankm product end charts and representatives; no empty-rank target problem is asserted.

boundaries.evidence: Step 3.1 proves actual constant representative indexzero by cancellation of its two verticalcaps.
The Statement and step 1.1 apply to a singleactual representative even when it is nonholomorphic.

boundaries.reason: The Statement requires transverse generators and exact product end charts; tangent or degenerate ends are not claimed.

boundaries.evidence: Steps 1.2 and 2.2 use one common pair of constanttails and fixedgenerator charts along the entire homotopy; step 4.1 exchanges them correctly under reversal.
Step 1.2 constructs a jointframe by one finitecover and one parameterdependent commutator series rather than choosing frames independently for everyhomotopy parameter.

No converse or continuousrelative smoothing theorem is asserted in the Statement.
